findings.reason: the stated endpoint is false as scoped, so §5 needs a clause on the write path (retarget the writers to DDv4 or move the DD3 factor to the census's member), which changes the deliverable and effort.
findings.text: §5 removes only the DD3 read path while nova's write path still converts to COCOS 11: nova/imas/sample.py:22 sets DEFAULT_DD_VERSION = "3.39.0" and line 352 applies dd_equilibrium_factor(dd_version, PSI_LIKE), pinned at -1.0 by tests/test_internal_cocos_sites.py::test_a_dd3_write_carries_the_flux_sign_flip; a worker can satisfy every §5 done-when clause and leave nova writing a second convention by default

findings.reason: §1's class rule gives convention conversion a destination while its scan cannot emit a row for that class outside nova/imas, so the census cannot evidence the class was classified and its member needs the algebra importers as a row source.
findings.text: §1's row sources cover nova/imas plus mast_*/diiid_*/machine_* modules anywhere and their importers, so a convention-conversion module outside nova/imas that imports the algebra but no machine module gets no row and no class: nova/io/sourcemap.py:53 imports nova_cocos and nova/equilibrium/convention.py:66 imports convention

response_events.note: §5 now removes the DD3 write path as well as the read path: every nova writer, sample and pulse-design included, writes DDv4, COCOS 17 only; a DD3 entry for a consumer is written by the member from nova's DDv4 entry; the DD3 write-sign test moves to the member or goes with the path. §5 effort 5 h to 6 h.
